```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Combine all the weekly Earnings

#All the states
state_initials <- c("AL", "AK", "AZ", "AR", "CA", "CO", "CT", "DE", "FL", "GA",
                    "HI", "ID", "IL", "IN", "IA", "KS", "KY", "LA", "ME", "MD",
                    "MA", "MI", "MN", "MS", "MO", "MT", "NE", "NV", "NH", "NJ",
                    "NM", "NY", "NC", "ND", "OH", "OK", "OR", "PA", "RI", "SC",
                    "SD", "TN", "TX", "UT", "VT", "VA", "WA", "WV", "WI", "WY")

weekly_earnings_all <- data.frame()

for (i in 1:length(state_initials)){
  name <- state_initials[i]
  new_data <- read_csv(paste0("../raw_data/weekly_earnings/", name, ".csv"), skip = 1) |>
    # Renames the columns
    rename(Date = 1, weekly_earnings = 2) |>
    mutate(State = name)
  weekly_earnings_all <- bind_rows(weekly_earnings_all, new_data)}

# Split date into year and month
weekly_earnings_all <- weekly_earnings_all |>
  mutate(Year = year(Date),
         Month = month(Date)) |>
  select(-Date)

# Adjust weekly earnings to September 2026 dollars
CPI <- read.csv("../raw_data/CPIAUCNS.csv") |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(observation_date),
         Year = year(Date),
         Month = month(Date))

#Adjusting for CPI
CPI_base <- CPI |>
  filter(Date == as.Date("2026-09-01")) |>
  pull(CPIAUCNS)

weekly_earnings_all <- weekly_earnings_all |>
  left_join(CPI |> select(Year, Month, CPIAUCNS), by = c("Year", "Month")) |>
  mutate(real_weekly_earnings = weekly_earnings * (CPI_base / CPIAUCNS)) |>
  filter(!is.na(CPIAUCNS)) |>
  select(-CPIAUCNS)

#Save
write_csv(weekly_earnings_all, "../data/weekly_earnings_all.csv")

```

Declan
```{r}
#Read Data
gas_raw <- read.csv("../raw_data/MasterGas.csv")
CPI <- read.csv("../raw_data/CPIAUCNS.csv")
#Convert into datatime
gas_cleaned <- gas_raw |>
  mutate(
    Date = as.Date(Date),
    across(
      c(Regular, Mid.Grade, Premium, Diesel),
      parse_number))

# source for `across()`: https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/across.html
# Wrangling a new dataframe which contains the average monthly price 
# for each gasoline type in nominal terms 

gas_price_averages <- gas_cleaned |>
  mutate(
    month = floor_date(
      Date,
      unit = "month"),) |>
  group_by(month, State) |>
  summarise(
    MNA_Regular = mean(Regular, na.rm = TRUE),
    MNA_Mid.Grade = mean(Mid.Grade, na.rm = TRUE),
    MNA_Premium = mean(Premium, na.rm = TRUE),
    MNA_Diesel = mean(Diesel, na.rm = TRUE))

# Mutating the CPI date variable to be compatible with the date variable
# in the gas price dataframe

CPI_cleaned <- CPI |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(observation_date),)

# Extract base-month CPI
CPI_base <- CPI_cleaned |>
  filter(Date == as.Date("2026-09-01")) |>
  pull(CPIAUCNS)

# Join CPI to monthly gas prices
gas_cpi <- gas_price_averages |>
  left_join(CPI_cleaned, by = c("month" = "Date"))

# Calculate inflation-adjusted prices
gas_real <- gas_cpi |>
  mutate(
    MRA_Regular = MNA_Regular * (CPI_base / CPIAUCNS),
    MRA_Mid.Grade = MNA_Mid.Grade * (CPI_base / CPIAUCNS),
    MRA_Premium = MNA_Premium * (CPI_base / CPIAUCNS),
    MRA_Diesel = MNA_Diesel * (CPI_base / CPIAUCNS))

#Exclude Oct 2025 (govt shutdown) and Oct 2026 (not published yet)
gas_real_complete <- gas_real |>
  filter(!is.na(CPIAUCNS))

#Save
write_csv(gas_real_complete, "../data/gas_real.csv")
```

```{r}
# Import Massachusetts unemployment data
MA <- read_csv("../raw_data/unemployment/MA.csv")

# Create an empty dataframe
unemployment_all <- data.frame()

# Loop through all 50 states
for (i in 1:length(state_initials)) {
  # Identify the state
  name <- state_initials[i]
  # Import the state's unemployment data
  new_data <- read_csv(
    paste0("../raw_data/unemployment/", name, ".csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    #renaming the columns for date and unemployment rate.   
    rename(Date = 1,unemployment_rate = 2) |>
    mutate(State = name)
  
# Add the state's data to the combined dataframe
  unemployment_all <- bind_rows(
    unemployment_all,
    new_data)}

# Create Year and Month columns to standardize the format
unemployment_all <- unemployment_all |>
  mutate(
    Date = as.Date(Date),
    Year = year(Date),
    Month = month(Date))

# Check for missing unemployment observations
# October 2025 is missing for all 50 states
unemployment_all |>
  filter(is.na(unemployment_rate)) |>
  select(State, Date, unemployment_rate)

#filter out the NA 
unemployment_complete <- unemployment_all |>
  filter(!is.na(unemployment_rate))
#Save
```


```{r}
# Create an empty dataframe
labor_force_all <- data.frame()

# Loop through all 50 states
for (i in 1:length(state_initials)) {
  # Identify the state
  name <- state_initials[i]
  # Import the state's labor force participation
  new_data <- read_csv(
    paste0("../raw_data/labor_force_participation/", name, ".csv"),
    show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    #renaming the columns for date and labor force participation
    rename(Date = 1,
      labor_force_participation_rate = 2) |>
    mutate(State = name)
  # Add the state's data to the combined dataframe
  labor_force_all <- bind_rows(
    labor_force_all,
    new_data)}

# Create Year and Month columns
labor_force_all <- labor_force_all |>
  mutate(
    Date = as.Date(Date),
    Year = year(Date),
    Month = month(Date)) |>
  select(-Date)

# Check missing values
colSums(is.na(labor_force_all))

# Remove missing observations
labor_force_all <- labor_force_all |>
  filter(!is.na(labor_force_participation_rate))

#Save
write_csv(labor_force_all,
  "../data/labor_force_participation_all.csv")
```

Combining:
```{r}
#read all the csv files
unemployment <- unemployment_complete
gas <- gas_real_complete
weekly_earning <- weekly_earnings_all
weekly_hours <- weekly_hours_all


gas <- gas |>
  mutate(
    Year = year(month),
    Month = month(month))

#used different identifier for the states
unique(gas$State)
unique(unemployment$State)
unique(weekly_earning$State)

#standardized the state identifier
gas <- gas |>
  mutate(State = state.abb[match(State, state.name)]) |>
  filter(!is.na(State)) #need to remove DC since only gas has DC identified alone 

# Check duplicates in each dataset
unemployment |> count(State, Year, Month) |> filter(n > 1)
gas |> count(State, Year, Month) |> filter(n > 1)
weekly_earning |> count(State, Year, Month) |> filter(n > 1)
weekly_hours |> count(State, Year, Month) |> filter(n > 1)
#There were no duplicates

# Combine all four datasets
combined_data <- gas |>
  left_join(
    unemployment,
    by = c("State", "Year", "Month")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    weekly_earning,
    by = c("State", "Year", "Month")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    weekly_hours,
    by = c("State", "Year", "Month")
  )

#After checking combined data realized multiple dates so deciding only 1 of it
combined_data <- combined_data |>
  select(-month, -observation_date, -Date)

#final quality check
colSums(is.na(combined_data))

#Save
write_csv(combined_data, "../data/combined_data.csv")
```
